explanation.text: Time to combine the whole module. You will build a **message sorter**. It takes customer messages (fake ones) and sorts them into labels: `billing`, `shipping`, `technical` or `other`. The model is a parameter, so you test with a fake model and later use a real one.
The pipeline has five small steps. You build one function in each exercise:

items: `classify(model, message)`: ask the model, read the JSON, check the label.
`classify_with_retry(model, message, tries)`: try again if the answer is bad.
`sort_messages(model, messages)`: group all messages by label.

explanation.text: Each exercise gives you the earlier functions, so you can focus on one step.
The fake model in the first example reads only the text **after** `Message:`. The prompt also lists every label, so reading the whole prompt would match every word.
The sorter must never crash. A bad reply becomes `"unknown"`, and you can read the unknown ones yourself.

explanation.title: use a real model for your sorter
explanation.text: Save your pipeline functions in sorter.py. Add the ask_claude function from lesson 5. Start with 5 fake messages and read the "unknown" ones yourself.
explanation.code:
# at the bottom of sorter.py
messages = [
    "I was charged twice this month",
    "My parcel has not arrived",
    "The app closes when I open it",
    "Can I change my email address?",
    "Thanks, all good now!",
]

groups = sort_messages(ask_claude, messages)   # was: sort_messages(fake_model, messages)
print(make_report(groups))
for label, items in groups.items():
    print(label, items)

quiz.question: Why does `classify` return "unknown" for a bad reply and not crash?
options: Model output can be wrong, so the program must survive it
quiz.explanation: Model output is not trusted. A safe value keeps the program running, and you can check the unknown ones yourself.

quiz.question: What is the benefit of passing the model as a parameter?
options: You can swap a fake for a real model without changing the other code
quiz.explanation: The sorter only calls `model(prompt)`. Any function with the same shape works, fake or real.

quiz.question: Before you run this sorter with a real model on real customer messages, what should you do?
options: Get permission and check the privacy rules, and test with fake data first
Put your key in the code
quiz.explanation: Customer messages are private. Test with fake data and only send real data when you are allowed to.
